summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' challenge at START Hack Munich by analysing Soony's launch data, then building an alert agent (watcher, mail, phone calls, PWA push with GPT-Realtime voice) that finds problems and acts on them with human approval.
summary.outcome: Found the real launch risks (art books, statues, game cards, sleeves) and built a poller, versioned store, dashboard, supplier mail, Twilio/OpenAI voice alerts, a PWA with push and cookie login, real verifier cards in the inbox, and was wiring supplier replies back into cards. Several branches are committed locally but not pushed.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no notifications or webhooks; files are replaced under the same name, so the only change detection is polling and comparing SHA-256 checksums.

Challenge data is confidential: it lives in gitignored data/, and the CLAUDE.md rules are no em dashes, placeholders like example.com in tests and docs, no attribution trailers, and ask before every push to the private team repo.

Akshat's dashboard on branch akshat/dashboard shows only fixture cards (with supplier-one.example.com addresses) until a module writes real cards to data/store/*cards*.json; origin/integration/verifier produces real cards with to_email from the portal profiles.

The serve tmux session runs code from jonas/alerts while the working tree is jonas/voice-dashboard, which lacks alerts and openai_calls; restarting serve from this checkout would break the call webhooks.
BasicAuth must read ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD from the process env, not .env, otherwise Akshat's 12 tests fail.
The Twilio trial accepts only Url mode (no inline Twiml) and needs verified numbers; German and Belgian numbers need a business regulatory bundle, so a US number was used.

The OpenAI Realtime SIP webhook (realtime.call.incoming) is configured on the project page, not the organization page; noise handling needed server_vad threshold 0.8, near_field noise reduction, interrupt_response false and English-only transcription.

code.finding: Replaced browser basic-auth dialog with a /login page and a 30-day cookie, because iPhone home-screen PWAs get a blank 401 page and do not keep basic-auth credentials.

Transcript order fixed by inserting a placeholder line when the user stops speaking; hold-to-talk was tried and removed at the user's request; hang-up is meant to wait until the assistant finishes speaking.
Web Push with VAPID keys stored in data/state; subscriptions are dropped on 404/410; the manifest link needs crossorigin="use-credentials" behind auth.

Voice tools get_card_details, send_supplier_email and escalate_to: send only goes out after an explicit confirmed:true, only unedited prewritten drafts, and only to supplier addresses from the portal profiles.
New module that feeds supplier replies back onto cards via Akshat's existing reply field in actions.json.

workflow: Subagents are useful for cross-checking large document sets, such as 200 order confirmations and 59 scans against SAP, but their outputs must stay local when the data is confidential.
Because Entire only creates a checkpoint when repo files change, an early read-only session shows no checkpoints even though the hooks fired.
Confirm every paid action before taking it: a script auto-bought a US number without asking after the German purchase failed, and the user objected.
Test the data flow end to end through the tunnel after each change; real-device behaviour (iPhone PWA) still needs the user to test it.

friction: Portal token was initially empty, so the API returned 401 until the user added it.
Cloudflare tunnel setup hit several problems: the hostname was attached to the wrong tunnel, a second-level subdomain had a cert error, and QUIC was blocked (fixed with http2).
Twilio trial limits, KYC and the regulatory bundle blocked a German number; the US number costs about $0.38/min to a German mobile.
The real alert email went to a real address by accident until emails were made opt-in.
Voice noise problems: responses were cancelled, background chatter was answered and shown as Chinese text, and the assistant was cut off at the end of the call.
The PWA showed a white screen on reopen because of basic-auth 401.
GitHub was unreachable at one point, so work from that night was not pushed.
The user pushed a commit and later asked about hooks and checkpoints; the hook behaviour looked like a failure because no checkpoint was written.
open_items: Push jonas/alerts (5 commits) and jonas/voice-dashboard (several commits) only after the user's explicit OK, and tell Akshat about the branch.
Merge onto one branch with the team's integration/verifier before the demo, then restart serve from a branch that has both alerts and the dashboard.
Wire critical cards automatically to push, then to a Twilio and GPT-Realtime call if nobody answers within N minutes.
Finish and verify supplier replies attached to cards (replies.py poller), check whether Hwaseong has replied, and test the hang-up-after-speech fix.
Possibly add a revise_draft tool so the draft mail can be changed in the conversation.
Karton Nowak art book order is still not sent (the offer was valid for 24 h); Boise is resolved.
Hand-in by Sun 12:00: demo script, deck, video of 3 minutes or less, README paragraph on the alert agent and a deployed prototype.
PWA hold-to-talk-free voice, English transcription and the cookie login are untested on a real iPhone.
Ask the Lio engineers whether portal data is identical across teams and whether supplier replies create portal files.
